delay parameter τMG determines the characteristic mem-
ory timescale and the dynamical complexity of the gener-
ated sequence. Throughout this work, we set βMG = 0.2,
γMG = 0.1, and τMG = 18, for which the system ex-
hibits chaotic dynamics.
The equation is numerically
integrated using a fourth-order Runge–Kutta method.
After discarding an initial transient to ensure that the
trajectory has converged to the chaotic attractor, the so-
lution is sampled at a temporal interval of δtsamp = 3
to obtain the discrete sequence x(nδtsamp). The sampled
data are then linearly rescaled to the interval [−1, 1] to
produce the driving sequence {sn} injected into the quan-
tum reservoir. After removing the transient, the resulting
sequence is approximately stationary over the sampled
time window, with an approximately zero mean and a
nearly time-invariant variance. Its Fourier power spec-
trum exhibits a broadband continuous distribution with
a pronounced low-frequency peak, reflecting the coexis-
tence of a characteristic oscillation timescale and chaotic
temporal fluctuations. Additional statistical and spectral
analyses of the generated time series are provided in the
Supplementary Information.

matches.doc_title: CRexit observed: probing cosmic ray transport in the circumgalactic medium with absorption line spectra
matches.excerpt:
For the present study, we analyze the simulations introduced in
Weber et al. (2025) and post-process them to generate synthetic
absorption-line spectra. In the following, we briefly summarize
the relevant aspects of the numerical setup and describe the mod-
eling procedure used to connect the simulations to observable
CGM diagnostics.

matches.doc_title: Design of an Electrically Tunable Microtoroid for Frequency Selection of Polarization-Entangled Photons
matches.excerpt:
The whispering gallery mode spectrum was calculated using axisymmetric COMSOL eigenmode
simulations. The horizontal (H)-like and vertical (V)-like mode families were identified by
following each resonance as the mode order changed and by confirming their field distributions
and confinement near the resonator rim. The nine selected resonances were then recalculated
using progressively finer computational meshes to verify numerical convergence. The fine mesh
was used for all reported results because further mesh refinement produced only negligible
changes in the H–V resonance splitting compared with the loaded optical linewidth.

matches.doc_title: Depth-Efficient Quantum Topological Data Analysis for Regime-Specific Detection of Financial Stress
matches.excerpt:
In accordance with IEEE policy, we disclose that large lan-
guage models were used only for writing assistance (clarifying
prose and phrasing). All technical content, results, code, and
figures were produced and verified by the authors; no AI
system generated experimental data or numerical results. The
authors take full responsibility for the accuracy, originality, and
integrity of the submission, including every cited reference.

PPF does not necessarily require the existence of UPOs
(and, by extension, deterministic chaos) and can be used

I have enough from the corpus search (all 100 documents were covered, keyword mode). Here's the complete answer.

## Answer: Numerical simulation methods in the corpus

There is no single paper in this 100-document corpus dedicated to "numerical simulation methods" as a subject. Instead, the phrase surfaces as the *methodology* each of several physics papers uses. Here are the distinct numerical simulation methods that appear, with document and page for each.

**1. Fourth-order Runge–Kutta time integration** — *Thermodynamics of Quantum Reservoir Computing* (`2607.02157`), **p. 12.** The Mackey–Glass delay equation (parameters β=0.2, γ=0.1, τ=18, chaotic regime) is "numerically integrated using a fourth-order Runge–Kutta method," with an initial transient discarded so the trajectory converges to the chaotic attractor before sampling. This is the most explicit classical ODE-integration method in the corpus. (The paper also refers to "full numerical details" for its quantum-thermodynamic evaluations on p. 7.)

**2. Finite-element eigenmode simulation with mesh-convergence testing** — *Design of an Electrically Tunable Microtoroid…* (`2607.03437`), **p. 12.** Whispering-gallery-mode spectra were "calculated using axisymmetric COMSOL eigenmode simulations." Resonances were recalculated on "progressively finer computational meshes to verify numerical convergence," with the fine mesh adopted once further refinement changed results negligibly — a textbook mesh-refinement convergence procedure.

**3. Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations, post-processed into observables** — two astrophysics papers:
- *CRexit observed: probing cosmic ray transport in the CGM…* (`2607.06744`), **p. 1** (keywords list "Methods: numerical") and **p. 3**, where existing simulations are "post-process[ed]… to generate synthetic absorption-line spectra," connecting the numerical setup to CGM diagnostics.
- *Unravelling Turbulence and Magnetic Fields in Galaxy Clusters…* (`2607.06346`), **p. 12**, which tests "theoretical predictions from numerical MHD simulations," e.g. anisotropic magnetic-field amplification and Alfvén-wave–driven turbulent dissipation.

**4. Numerical simulation of spatiotemporal-chaos control** — untitled cardiac-dynamics paper (`0710.2265`), **p. 4.** Global control schemes for suppressing fibrillation are shown to work "at least in numerical simulations," by adding an external control signal A to the Panfilov reaction–diffusion model equations.

**5. Quantum-circuit / algorithm simulation** — two quantum-computing papers:
- *Open-boundary integrable quantum circuits…* (`2607.02093`), **p. 4**, discussing circuits "whose dynamics can be simulated efficiently on classical computers" (free-fermion / integrable-Trotterization).
- *Depth-Efficient Quantum Topological Data Analysis…* (`2607.09906`), **p. 3**, reporting "MaxCut numerical simulations" (m = 7000) and LABS-instance simulations up to N = 44–45.

**6. First-principles (DFT) simulation** — untitled polymer paper (`0802.0539`), **p. 3**, which used the "ab initio pseudopotential method within the DFT and the supercell formalism," modeling the system as an infinite chain — a numerical electronic-structure simulation.

### Summary
The corpus spans, in order of how directly each matches "numerical simulation methods":
- **ODE integration** (Runge–Kutta) — `2607.02157` p. 12
- **Finite-element eigenmode + mesh convergence** (COMSOL) — `2607.03437` p. 12
- **MHD simulations** — `2607.06744` pp. 1, 3 and `2607.06346` p. 12
- **Reaction–diffusion chaos-control simulation** — `0710.2265` p. 4
- **Quantum-circuit/algorithm simulation** — `2607.02093` p. 4, `2607.09906` p. 3
- **DFT/ab-initio simulation** — `0802.0539` p. 3

If you meant a specific method (e.g. only Runge–Kutta, or only finite-element/COMSOL), tell me which and I'll pull the full method section from that paper with page-level detail.

*Note: semantic search was unavailable (fastembed not installed), so this ran as keyword search; a genuinely fuzzy match like "computational modeling" phrasing that never uses the words "numerical"/"simulation" could have been missed.*
